title: Measured axon length gives only three direction-discordant pairs per species in selected Allen slices
abstract: We tested whether longer measured axon truncation distance predicts more detected outputs than inputs in Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1. Both cells in each pair had the same broad cell class and the same truncated or borderline axon label. No lengths were imputed. There were 140 mouse VisP pairs and 52 human TCx pairs. Each species had only three pairs with a connection detected in one direction alone, from two inferred donors. All 87 truncated-group pairs had no detected connection in either direction. Longer-minus-shorter direction contrasts were -2.14 and -1.92 percentage points. Exact donor sign-change reference p values were 0.50 and 1.00 under a symmetry assumption. Sparse donor contributions made bootstrap intervals unreliable for population inference. The result does not establish equal rates or refute axon preservation corrections. It extends a prior category-only audit to measured length within a fixed label. Code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External records are not bundled.

display.caption: Paired detection contrasts and nominal 97.5% donor bootstrap intervals. Sparse donor support can make intervals too narrow. Zero-width intervals do not establish equal rates.
